title: Anisotropy invariant map (Lumley triangle)
summary: A plot of the second and third invariants of the Reynolds-stress anisotropy tensor inside a curvilinear triangle. Each point is a state of the turbulence: isotropic at the bottom corner, one-component at the top, two-component along the curved edge.

media.alt: Anisotropy invariant map showing a curvilinear triangle with corners labelled isotropic, axisymmetric contraction and one-component, and a coloured path from the wall to the centre.
media.caption: Reference render with synthetic demonstration data (design-system gallery).

source.note: Plot class from the design system's plot taxonomy; synthetic demonstration data.

read_the_figure.question: What is the state of the Reynolds stress?
read_the_figure.axes: x: xi, the third-invariant coordinate (dimensionless, about -1/6 to 1/3). y: eta, the second-invariant coordinate (0 to about 1/3). Colour: wall distance (normalised).
look_at: Does every point lie inside the triangle? Realisable turbulence cannot lie outside.
Where does the path start (wall, ringed) and where does it end (centre)?
Which edge or corner is the path close to near the wall?
Does the path follow the right edge (axisymmetric expansion) or the curved one (two-component)?
read_the_figure.proves: It shows which kind of anisotropy the turbulence has at each position: how close it is to isotropic, two-component or one-component. A model that cannot reproduce the path from DNS cannot reproduce the stress anisotropy.
if_wrong: Points outside the triangle: the model is not realisable.
Bounds not drawn: no way to tell what is possible.
No colour or arrow for position: the path has no direction.

terms.meaning: b_ij = <u_i u_j> / (2k) - delta_ij / 3; zero for isotropic turbulence.
xi = (b_ij b_jk b_ki / 6)^(1/3), eta = (b_ij b_ji / 6)^(1/2); independent of the axes chosen.
Constraint that the Reynolds-stress tensor is positive semi-definite, which fixes the triangle.
Limits: equal fluctuations in all directions; fluctuation in one direction only; none in one direction.
Mean of products of velocity fluctuations, <u_i u_j>, the stress from turbulent momentum transport.

remember: Isotropic: xi = eta = 0. One-component: xi = eta = 1/3. Two-component, axisymmetric: xi = -1/6, eta = 1/6.
Straight edges eta = |xi| are axisymmetric states; the curved edge is the two-component limit eta^2 = 1/27 + 2 xi^3.
The path from wall to centre is the main feature.

understand.title: Marks and encodings
understand.text: Position in the plane encodes the anisotropy state. The white outline is the realisable region; the corner labels name the limiting states. Points are coloured by normalised wall distance (dark at the wall to yellow at the centre), the line joining them gives the order, and the amber ring flags the wall point.

understand.title: Why this form answers the question
understand.text: The Reynolds-stress tensor has six components that depend on the axes. Two invariants collapse it to a point in a plane that has the same meaning in every coordinate system, and the realisability bound frames all possible states in one triangle. The path from wall to centre is then a curve to compare with DNS or another model.

understand.title: Read this reference render
understand.text: Q1: Where does the path begin? At the wall (ringed), at about xi = 0.30, eta = 0.30, almost at the one-component corner: near a wall turbulence has mostly streamwise fluctuations. Q2: Where does it end? Near the centre it moves to about xi = -0.08, eta = 0.085, near the left (axisymmetric contraction) edge close to the isotropic corner, so turbulence there is much more isotropic. Q3: Is every point inside? Yes: all 14 points are inside the outline and the first few hug the right and upper edges.

understand.title: The must-check list, explained
understand.text: Triangle bounds drawn: the outline is the content of realisability. Without it the viewer cannot see how close a state is to the limit or whether a model violates it.

understand.title: How it misleads
understand.text: Invariants lose information: different stress tensors with equal xi and eta look identical, and the map says nothing about the magnitude of the turbulence. A path drawn without markers hides that few points define it. Many readers do not know which corner is which. Points near an edge are hard to separate, and the scale is compressed near the vertex.

understand.title: Alternatives
understand.text: Plot the Reynolds-stress components as profiles. Use the barycentric map (equilateral triangle) where the three limiting states are equally spaced. Use eigenvalues of b_ij on a ternary diagram.

understand.title: A variant to create
understand.text: Draw the barycentric version side by side and add a DNS path in a second colour.

steps.title: Anisotropy tensor and its invariants
steps.note: k is the turbulent kinetic energy; b is traceless.

worked.title: Where does a near-wall stress state land?
worked.problem: At a station <uu> = 0.8, <vv> = 0.1, <ww> = 0.1 (units of m^2/s^2, no shear). Find xi and eta.

solution.text: k = 0.5 times the trace; b is diagonal.

worked.answer: xi = eta = 0.233, on the right straight edge (axisymmetric expansion): strongly streamwise.

analyze.q: Why is the whole picture bounded by a triangle?
The model path is a straight line from the isotropic corner. What could that mean about the closure?
analyze.hint: Think of a linear eddy-viscosity model.

evaluate.q: Is it enough to match the path on this map to say the model reproduces the Reynolds stresses?
evaluate.hint: What does the map not show?

create: Redraw on the barycentric map with the three limiting states at the corners.
Overlay a second path (another model) and colour both by wall distance.

checks.q: What does the corner xi = eta = 0 mean?
checks.hint: Think of equal fluctuations in all directions.

checks.q: A simulation has a point at xi = 0.3, eta = 0.2. What can you say?
checks.hint: Check the bounds of the triangle at xi = 0.3.
checks.answer: At xi = 0.3 the lower bound is eta = 0.3 (straight edge); eta = 0.2 is outside, so the Reynolds stresses are not realisable.
